premises.text: The web is fragmented across sites and single-purpose apps, forcing users to assemble information in stacks of tabs
premises.evidence_span: we've traded the fluidity and connectedness of surfing for stacks of browser tabs and single-purpose mobile apps

premises.text: VIRB weaves services into contextual cards and a persistent activity stream so users can plan and explore without leaving the page
premises.evidence_span: reinvent surfing the internet on web or mobile by weaving together services you use

premises.text: Semantic search, recommendations, and new UI paradigms build contextual bridges across services
premises.evidence_span: To build these contextual bridges across services, we use data technologies like semantic search and recommendations

premises.text: Activity syncs across web and mobile with deep links into other apps and shared collections with notifications
premises.evidence_span: VIRB syncs my activity and data across devices

premises.text: Initial service graph focuses on places, movies, and media, with beta signup as the entry channel
premises.evidence_span: We're starting by connecting services around places, movies, and media

value.text: Users get things done in one place by fluidly surfing across interconnected services on any device
value.evidence_span: an intelligent layer over the internet that helps you get things done in one place

causal_links.evidence_span: why do we need to settle on a fragmented web?
bring back the magic of surfing, fluidly moving from link to link, service to service
connecting services around places, movies, and media

notes: Night-out planning and judge-graph demos treated as applications of one weaving mechanism (§4.1.2). Cards, streams, collections, share, deep links, and sync folded as feature cascade of that product (§4.1.7). Semantic search/recommendations kept with product as enabling tech of the same bridges. Beachhead categories + beta signup as separately revisable GTM module. Singleton D1/D3 retained. Anti-template: problem, product, and beachhead separately revisable. ASR VIRB/Verb left in spans.
